title: What a Heckuva Way to Die
transcription:
Gory, Gory, What a Heckuva-way to Die

"Will it reach around the chalkstone?"
cried the bolloyer looking up.
Our hero feebly answered "yes"
and slowly inched on up.
He was trying to drive a piton
when his foot hold crumbled up,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus:
Gory, Gory,
what a heckuva-way to die,
Gory, Gory,
what a heckuva-way to die,
Gory, Gory,
what a heckuva-way to die,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

He shot on down the chimney
and he quickly gathered speed,
he shot past the bolloyer
who'd forgot the climbers' creed.
An anchor to a piton would've
been all he'd ever need,
And he ain't gonna climb no more

Chorus

The bolloyer felt the rope run tight
and tried to let it run,
But it jerked him from position
and he knew his time had come.
He left the rock behind him
as he shot towards the sun,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus

The Medic in the valley
watched them through the telescope,
And as they neared the bottom
his eyes grew wide with hope;
For it had been a week or more
since the parting of the rope,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus

The hit the ground the sound was splat,
the blood was spurting high,
His comrades were heard to say:
"What a colorful way to die!"
And as they lay there writhing
in the welter and the gore,
He ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus

One had the rope around his neck,
a piton through his spleen,
An ice axe in the rucksack
had split the other's bean.
The trails of red marked their descent
as they neared the slopes of green,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus

There was blood upon the rucksack,
there were brains upon the rope,
Intestines were intertwined
in the green and grassy slope.
They scooped them up in a lunch pail
after salvaging the rope,
And he ain't gonna climb no more.

Chorus
